Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, Poland

Demolished. Ostrowiec's Jewish community, first settled in the 16th century, numbered 10,095 in 1921, most of them murdered by the Germans at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery, established no later than the mid-17th century, became a wartime execution site, with an estimated 2,000 victims buried there; burials continued as late as March 1945, and on May 11, 1947, the bodies of the Sztein family, murdered by a Pole just before the Red Army's arrival and hidden in a well, were also moved here. The cemetery was officially closed in 1955 and turned into a park around 1960. In 2018, at the initiative of Meir Bulka of the J-nerations organization, the ohel of tzaddik Meir Jechiel ha-Lewi Halsztok was rebuilt on the site.
